key_provisions_or_claims: Analyses whether smart robots are 'things' under Jordanian Civil Code Art. 291 (guardian liability) or 'products' under consumer protection and standards law.
Guardian liability requires proof of custody, which is hard to apply to autonomous robots.
Defective-product liability fits the robot's physical structure but not its autonomous 'mental' dimension.
Jordanian law lacks a definition of AI; general civil liability rules are inadequate.
Calls for a modern, clear legal framework allocating responsibility for robot-caused harm.
annotation.summary_en: Legal doctrinal article examining whether smart robots are 'things' or 'products' under Jordanian civil law (with French law comparison), and whether guardian liability or defective-product liability applies to robot-caused damage. It finds existing rules inadequate and calls for a modern legal framework clarifying responsibility.
annotation.title_clean: The Problem of Establishing Civil Liability for Harmful Effects of Smart Robots
annotation.title_en: The Problem of Establishing Civil Liability for Harmful Effects of Smart Robots
